text:
kevin: Created postmortem for the span-loss + aggregation drift incident. Root cause: batching window regression + late schema change in metrics join. Using this thread for owners/action items.

ops-bot: Postmortem uploaded: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/1912345678

maya: I'll own the ETL batching fix. Plan: tighten window semantics, add deterministic jitter seed, and add a regression unit test for edge-case windows. ETA: PR by Fri.

otto: I'll take aggregation reconciliation and schema guards. Plan: add defensive join handling, back-compat checks, and an end-to-end checksum test. ETA: early next week.

harper: I'll handle runbook+comms and the remediation tracker updates. Need concrete backfill scope before drafting customer notes.

kevin: Backfill estimate: ~5 hours of data across two high-volume tenants (~750k spans). Suggest canary tenant run first. Command pattern: `./tools/replay --start 2026-04-02T02:00Z --end 2026-04-02T07:00Z --tenant <id> --dry-run` then remove dry-run. Expect ~1.5h per tenant with rate cap.

maya: Local tests green; patch changes window inclusive bounds and caps burst size. PR: https://github.com/redwood/etl/pull/439 cc @otto for join impact.

otto: Added `agg.recon.mismatch` metric and `observability.dropped_spans`. Alert rules: dropped_spans > 0.15% over 10m -> page; agg.recon.mismatch > 0 -> page. Created dashboard tile: https://dashboards.internal/d/obs/1912345678

harper: Runbook snippet added: "If dropped_spans alert fires: rollback to last stable ETL, start backfill playbook, run checksum verification, notify CS." Comms draft in drive: https://docs.internal/incident-comms/1912345678

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: Mon 09:00  canary check-in meeting created.

maya: Deploying canary to 5% now. Monitoring latency and CPU.

otto: Canary signals look promising: dropped_spans fell from ~1.6% -> 0.04% on canary. Aggregation checksum sample matched on canary dataset.

harper: Updated remediation tracker with owners and ETAs: ETL fix -> maya (PR 439); Aggregation tests & schema guard -> otto (ticket INF-941); Runbook & comms -> harper. Target close date: 2026-04-10.

kevin: Noting recurrence pattern: windowing regressions have occurred twice this year. Recommend adding a monthly regression smoke test that simulates tail traffic and schema-evolution scenarios.

otto: Filed INF-942 to add monthly regression and long-term schema compatibility testing.

maya: After canary passes I'll open a short blameless summary and mark remaining infra items in the postmortem doc.

kevin: Thanks team. Keeping this thread as single-source follow-up.
